label: fw.wad, the mod's textures, judged as one set: a concrete wall, a wet concrete floor, a steel grate with holes, a catwalk floor, a pipe-covered wall, a hazard-striped trim, a rusted steel plate, a control panel with dials, a sodium lamp's face (lit), the water, a sign reading PUMP 3, a door

halfLifeDetail.band: T5's band is least to most, Half-Life's own from the 5th to the 95th in 100: fine detail inside it is Valve's own range (a quartile is no bound); under least reads smeared or flat, over most noisy. A texture the brief asks to be one plain colour is flat in Valve's too (its BLACK and YELLOW are 0): flat is right there, and T5 is 2

T1.reason: Most of the twelve-plus set is what the brief asks, but three fail it. The pipe-covered wall (FW_PIPEWALL) has one horizontal pipe and a short vertical strip at its right edge, not a wall covered in pipes. The control panel (FW_CONTROL) has glowing orange squares for dials, cut off at its right edge, and no visible screens or switches. The sign (FW_PUMP3) reads 'PUMP' with no '3'.

T2.reason: Judged by eye, since no map-view colour measure was given: concrete grey, wet floor and water green-grey, the hazard yellow and black, the rust plate blue-grey with orange rust, the sodium face orange, the pump sign yellow, the door green. These match the brief's words. The map-view check was not run here, so this rests on the flat sheet.

T3.reason: The pipe wall's layout does not match the brief's pipe-covered wall: one pipe band where the brief asks for many pipes across the surface. The control panel's dial rows are placed so the right-hand dial is cut at the tile edge, so it does not line up as a panel. The other tiles, the rust plate's 4x4 plates and the tile floor's grid, are at plausible wall scale.

T4.reason: Not a must item. The control panel's cut dial at the right edge (x about 370 to 383 on the sheet) will meet the next repeat of the tile's left edge as a visible seam. The pipe wall's right-edge brown strip also reads as a seam. The concrete, grate and tile repeat cleanly.

T5.reason: FW_HAZARD measures 153.9 fine detail against Half-Life's band of 10.8 to 75: it is noisy, a dense diagonal hatch that reads as static at this size. FW_SODIUM (5.4), FW_WATER (3.2) and FW_WETFLOOR (9.1) are below the band and read flat or smeared, and the sodium and water are not briefed as plain colours. FW_YARD (9.5) is also under. Concrete (28.1), grate (42), rust plate (20.7), control (25.9), tile (26.3) and the door (14.9) sit within the band and look sharp.

T6.reason: Names and sizes all match the measured list, and '{FW_GRATE' and '!FW_WATER' carry their prefixes. The sodium face is lit, and the water is a liquid-looking surface. But FW_PUMP3's name means a sign reading 'PUMP 3', and the sign reads only 'PUMP'. The grate's holes are dark gaps on the flat sheet, so whether they are transparent holes cannot be confirmed from the picture.
